newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore couples rush to marry ahead of flat levy.
newsitem.headline: Singapore couples rush to marry ahead of flat levy.

text.p: Couples in Singapore are rushing to the altar to avoid paying a hefty deposit for a public housing apartment, The Straits Times reported on Friday.
Singapore's new measures to curb speculation in the housing requires unmarried couples waiting to buy a flats to fork out a Singapore $5,000 (US$3,500) deposit by the July 12 deadline.
However, under the new rules they can avoid paying the levy if they show they are married before that date.
The government brought in the the levy to deter "frivolous applications", which would push those in genuine need of housing back in the queue.
Couples often wait up to five years for government-built apartments, which house some 90 percent of Signapore's three million people.
